summary_sentences.text: User requires no production restarts and local reproduction of the memory leak.
Assistant creates a load test with 500 concurrent clients that send messages and reconnect in a churn loop.
During the churn test, RSS grows ~65 MB per minute and heapUsed follows, indicating a JavaScript heap leak.
A heap snapshot diff shows large deltas of WebSocket, Timeout, closures, and strings, suggesting listener or cache retention.
User instructs to start with listener theory and requires a minimum 10-minute soak test before calling any fix effective.
Auditing listener registration sites in the codebase highlights per-connection listeners on the socket in connection.js.
During churn, listener counts on shared emitters (wss, bus, process) stay constant at 1, showing no accretion.
A search for MaxListenersExceededWarning in local and production logs yields no matches.
Because no evidence of listener leak on shared emitters and no Node warnings, the listener theory is deprioritized and cache investigation begins.
Code search reveals a messageCache Map in cache.js without any eviction logic, causing unbounded growth.
The cache is intended for redelivery but lacks a limit, so all relayed messages are retained indefinitely.
An LRU cap of 50k entries and a 5-minute TTL are added to messageCache, configurable via environment variables.
After the cache fix, the memory leak slope drops to ~27 MB/min but a linear growth remains, indicating another leak.
Heap retainer analysis reveals heartbeat.js leaks a repeating setInterval and accumulates 'pong' listeners on per-socket emitters, retaining disconnected sockets.
The code silenced Node's warning with setMaxListeners(0), which prevented detection of the listener pile-up.
The fix registers a single persistent 'pong' listener, clears the interval on socket close, and removes setMaxListeners(0).
Per-socket instrumentation shows exactly one 'pong' listener on each live socket during churn.
After all clients disconnect and a forced GC, interval count drops to zero and WebSocket instances drop to 3, compared to ~14,000 before the fix.
A 15-minute soak test with 500 churning clients yields a flat memory profile (0.02 MB/min slope), confirming the leak is resolved.
A CI leak-guard regression test is added to prevent future regressions.
User requests a summary of the incident and PR description, including explanation of why the initial listener investigation missed the leak.

Assistant provides a summary detailing the two root causes: the heartbeat timer/listener leak and the unbounded message cache, and notes how setMaxListeners(0) and per-socket emitters hid the listener leak.
